summary: Repository set up from the project brief: knowledge base, data files and dashboard created.
Dashboard redesigned to be easier to follow: this week's jobs up front, plain-English reasons for each job, must-have checklists, and jargon explained on tap.
Added Sky Barrage, a SmartMotion arcade game with 20 levels, in a new Games section of the dashboard.
Added the Print & Design workspace: a 3D model library with 3D views, downloads (STL + STEP), print settings and lessons. Three starter models for the rig: button box, cable clip and VR headset hook.
Dashboard rebuilt as a website for Cloudflare Pages: app icon and phone home-screen support, normal file downloads, and a build that checks the data before every deploy.
Version 1.1.0: the dashboard now shows whether you're signed in (and warns in red if the website has no login protection), and shows its version number under the logo.

Version 1.2.0: new game SmartMotion Flight, a flight simulator-style game around Duxford with SmartMotion signs, a trainer and a WW2 fighter, a gate race, phone, laptop and Meta Quest (VR) support, and motion telemetry for the simulator rig.

Version 1.3.0: SmartMotion Flight now also exists as a native Windows game (built with the Godot engine) that uses the PC's graphics card, with Meta Quest 3 VR over Link and a direct UDP link to the motion rig. It is built automatically and published as a download.

Version 1.4.0: Sam flew the native game in VR on the Quest 3 for the first time; it worked but was hard to control. Flying is now easier (Easy mode sets full power on the runway, power keys respond three times faster, WASD flies in VR too, the right trigger adds power on the Quest controller) and the graphics are better (puffy clouds, a richer sky, proper trees across the countryside, more ground detail, softer light and shadows).

Version 1.5.0: the native SmartMotion Flight game now flies over the real Duxford area, built from free open data: real ground heights (Copernicus DEM), a real satellite photo of the ground (Copernicus Sentinel-2), 129,000 real buildings including the Duxford hangars (Overture Maps / OpenStreetMap), real woods (ESA WorldCover) with trees streamed in as you fly, close-up ground and building textures (ambientCG, free for any use), and 3D clouds you can fly through with shadows on the ground. The runway now has its real heading (058) and length. Credits and licences are recorded (LIC-10 to LIC-14).

Version 1.6.0: you now fly Skysmart's own Scottish Aviation Bulldog (G-SMAT, ex-RAF XX658) in the native game, built from the real dimensions and performance figures, in RAF trainer colours, with a detailed 3D cockpit for VR: live round gauges behind glass, moving control sticks, pedals and levers, seats, canopy frames and an instructor in the right-hand seat. The paint is an assumption until we have photos of the aircraft as it is now.

Version 1.6.1, ready for the VR test: a menu inside the headset (X opens it; stick and A to choose) to change aircraft, start, mode, time of day and Easy/Pro, recentre or leave VR, so no keyboard is needed. Fixed: the controllers didn't work while paused or after a crash (X paused but couldn't resume), and STALL/PULL UP warnings stayed in the headset. VR is also sharper when you turn your head.

Version 1.6.2: smoother flying (buildings and trees now load in the background, so no more stutters when new scenery appears), sharper shadows in the cockpit, a lighter instrument panel, and a cleaner cockpit view on the laptop screen. New automatic check for the scenery loading.

Version 1.6.3: smoother VR. Looking around in the headset stuttered because the game couldn't keep up with the headset. Now the instrument panel's fixed parts are drawn once instead of every frame, shadows in VR are simpler and shorter-range, the picture edges are drawn in less detail (foveated rendering), anti-aliasing is 2x instead of 4x in VR, the headset is asked for a steady 72 Hz (changeable in the in-headset menu, which also shows the frame rate), Quest Link gets depth information so late frames don't warp the cockpit, and scenery loading is spread over more frames. The diagnostics log now records frame timing in VR.

Version 1.6.4: fixes VR not starting in 1.6.3 (the headset stayed on Quest Link's loading hourglass). Foveated rendering, sending depth to the headset and the automatic 72 Hz request are taken out again; the smoother instrument panel, lighter VR shadows, 2x anti-aliasing and spread-out scenery loading stay. The refresh rate can still be changed from the in-headset menu.

Version 1.7.0: in VR you now sit firmly in the seat (the headset was placed one frame behind the aircraft, so the cockpit wobbled around your head in flight), you have gloved hands instead of orange blocks (the right hand closes around the control stick and moves with it, the left takes the throttle), and the game lowers the picture resolution a little by itself whenever the graphics card can't keep up, so it stays smooth.

Version 1.7.1: the Games tile for SmartMotion Flight now gives the Windows download (always the latest) with step-by-step instructions, and explains that you can simply ask Claude in a Claude Code session for the latest link. The browser version of the game is no longer on the website.
Parked idea added: a VR model viewer that turns a 2D component drawing into a 3D model you can inspect at real size in your room.

Version 1.8.0: SmartMotion Flight is now three games in one program, picked at the top of the menu. Racing: drive an open-wheel racing car in SmartMotion colours round a new 4 km circuit with kerbs, gravel, SmartMotion barrier boards, grandstands with crowds, pits and start lights; race seven computer cars over 3 laps or set a fast lap on your own. Space: fly a space fighter round a space station, an asteroid field, a ringed planet and a moon, and shoot down waves of drones. In VR the game's own menus now float in front of you (point and pull the trigger to click), so you can change game and settings without taking the headset off. Both new games drive the motion rig too.
